findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, making FromContext log calls unobservable in tests
findings.body: The new FromContext method on TestLogger ignores the receiver and returns a brand-new TestLogger instance. This PR changes LoggerMiddleware to emit its "Plugin Request Completed" log via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so any test that constructs the middleware with plog.NewTestLogger() and then asserts on InfoLogs/ErrorLogs of that instance will see zero recorded calls — the log entry is written to an unreachable instance. Tests verifying plugin request logging will either fail or (if written against the new behavior) silently assert nothing. FromContext should return f (or record on f and return it) so log calls made through FromContext remain assertable.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the moved log attributes have no test coverage
findings.body: This PR introduces ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which is now solely responsible for attaching endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname to the request context, and simultaneously removes those explicit fields from LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" log line. No test was added for the new middleware, and the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go only asserts prometheus metrics. Nothing verifies that the contextual attributes are actually injected or that the plugin egress log line still contains pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID, so a regression (middleware reordering, or a change in log.WithContextualAttributes / ConcreteLogger.FromContext behavior) would silently strip these identifying fields from plugin request logs.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running before it
findings.body: Previously LoggerMiddleware derived pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID itself from the request's PluginContext. After this change it relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) picking up attributes injected by the separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware, so the two middlewares are order-dependent: the stack in CreateMiddlewares must keep NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() before NewLoggerMiddleware(...). Neither constructor documents this coupling. Any other code path that builds its own middleware list (tests, alternate decorators, or a future reordering) will get "Plugin Request Completed" logs missing all plugin-identifying fields, with no error. The ordering requirement should be documented, or the fields kept in LoggerMiddleware.

findings.title: Explicit traceID attribute removed from plugin request completion logs
findings.body: The old logRequest implementation explicitly extracted the trace ID via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended it as the "traceID" field on the "Plugin Request Completed" log line. That code was deleted and replaced with m.logger.FromContext(ctx), so trace-log correlation for plugin egress logs now depends entirely on whether infra/log's ConcreteLogger.FromContext adds the trace ID from the context — behavior outside this diff and not covered by any test in this package. If FromContext does not add it, plugin request logs lose traceID and can no longer be correlated with traces.
